we propose a probabilistic SLAM system for real time dense depth reconstruction from monocular video, which is the first to use a learned compact depth representation and to unify three different types of error metrics within a factor graph framework, and that we demonstrate that this approach is competitive with state of the art SLAM methods in trajectory estimation and dense depth reconstruction.
we present the first dense monocular SLAM system that is able to run in real time and that is capable of estimating accurate trajectories and dense 3D geometry from monocular sequences.

we present a SLAM framework that unifies the use of learned depth map representations, photometric, reprojections and geometric errors, in a probabilistic formulation, and we show that this can be used in real time for monocular SLAM.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: - A new probabilistic SLAM system that combines the benefits of both sparse and dense representations. - A new compact representation for depth maps that can be efficiently updated and used within a factor graph framework.

we have developed a real-time monocular dense SLAM system that is capable of estimating dense geometry in real-time.
our method is able to produce high quality depth maps and camera trajectories from a single monocular camera.

our system is able to estimate dense geometry and trajectory in real time, while being more accurate than state-of-the-art methods, and more flexible than existing probabilistic methods, which only deal with sparse geometry.

our system is a real time dense monocular SLAM system which uses a compact learned representation and a novel probabilistic factorisation of the SLAM problem.
our system is able to achieve real time performance on monocular sequences while providing a compact representation of the scene and camera motion.

it is possible to combine different types of information and optimise a dense map representation with real-time performance.
